newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-SURHOFF KNOCKS IN SIX RUNS AS ORIOLES EDGE ANGELS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-SURHOFF KNOCKS IN SIX RUNS AS ORIOLES EDGE ANGELS.

text.p: B.J. Surhoff knocked in six
runs as the Baltimore Orioles rallied from a six-run deficit
to beat the Anaheim Angels 10-9 Saturday in a battle of
division leaders.
Surhoff, who entered the game in a 1-for-15 slump,
continued his prowess with the bases loaded as Baltimore
posted its biggest comeback win of the season. He delivered a
two-run single with the bases full in the fifth and cleared
the bases with a double one inning later.
"When you get down and you're able to pull the guys out of
a hole, it's nice to be able to come back," Surhoff said.
Surhoff, who also had an RBI double in the first, is
10-for-14 with 20 RBI with the bases loaded this season. In
his career, he is 52-for-113 (.460) with 134 RBI with the bags
full.
"I was just up in the right situations," he said. "The
guys ahead of me were doing the job. Nothing happens if they
don't get on base."
The Orioles' seven-run six inning was their biggest of the
season and helped them win for the 17th time in 23 games.
Baltimore also stretched its lead in the American League East
to 4 1/2 games over the second-place Yankees.
Arthur Rhodes (8-3) got the win, despite allowing three
runs and four hits in 3 1/3 innings. Randy Myers tossed a
scoreless ninth for his 36th save in 37 chances.
Dave Hollins had two doubles and a triple and drove in a
run for Anaheim, which fell a half game behind Seattle in the
A.L. West.
Jim Edmonds, Darin Erstad, Todd Greene and Tim Salmon
homered for Anaheim. Reliever Darrell May (0-1) took the loss.
In New York, former Yankees closer John Wetteland had an
RBI double in the middle of a three-run 10th inning and
pitched two hitless innings as the Texas Rangers won 8-5.
Wetteland, the World Series Most Valuable Player last year
who signed with the Rangers in the off-season, improved to 7-2
and got his first hit in over three years. Texas pitchers are
batting .333 (5-for-15) with a homer and four RBI this season.
"I was real excited about it," an emotional Wetteland
said. "I was wondering if I might not even get a chance to do
it (pitch at Yankee Stadium) this year. At least until I got
to the gate and stepped onto the field and heard what I
heard."
Wetteland heard boos, a far cry from the cheers he
triggered by recording the final out of the 1996 World Series.
"There was about a five-second span where I allowed myself
to explore my emotions ... and like I said, it was five
seconds to think about the last time I was here," he said. "I
have mixed emotions, some people just don't get it and that's
very sad."
Juan Gonzalez, who had three hits and three RBI, led off
the 10th with a single off Ramiro Mendoza (4-5), the fourth
New York pitcher. Ex-Yankee Jim Leyritz sacrificed and
pinch-hitter Domingo Cedeno snapped a 5-5 tie with an RBI
single.
Wetteland, forced into the lineup when designated hitter
Ivan Rodriguez was shifted to catcher, belted the first pitch
on one bounce off the left-field wall, plating Cedeno with his
first hit since June 14, 1994, when he was with Montreal. For
his career, he is hitting .167 with a homer and eight RBI.
In Chicago, Edgar Martinez hit his 20th homer and drove in
four runs, Jay Buhner smacked his 29th dinger and Paul
Sorrento added a three-run shot in a five-run seventh inning,
his 23rd, as the Seattle Mariners pounded the White Sox 11-6.
The second game of the doubleheader was postponed due to
rain. It will be made up as part of a doubleheader Sunday.
In Cleveland, Matt Williams and Marquis Grissom homered in
a six-run seventh inning as the Indians rallied for an 8-4
victory over the Toronto Blue Jays, their fourth straight win.
Reliever Paul Quantrill (5-5) yielded both homers after
having having allowed just four homers in 66 innings.
Jim Thome homered for the third straight game for the
Indians. In their last three games, the Tribe have outhomered
foes, 10-0.
Paul Shuey (3-1) pitched a career-high four innings of
one-hit relief for Cleveland, which opened a 5 1/2-game lead
over the White Sox and Brewers in the A.L. Central.
In Boston, Wil Cordero, Troy O'Leary and Bill Haselman
drove in two runs apiece as the Red Sox got their third
straight victory, a 12-4 rout of the Minnesota Twins.
John Valentin added three hits for Boston, which has won
nine of its last 13 games.
In Detroit, Kevin Appier allowed one run over eight
innings to win for the first time in nine starts and Bip
Roberts had a tie-breaking RBI single in the fifth as the
Kansas City Royals dealt the Tigers their fourth straight
loss, 2-1.
Appier (7-10) scattered eight hits -- four by Bobby
Higginson -- to break a personal five-game losing streak. He
struck out seven without a walk.
In Milwaukee, Dave Nilsson's two-out single in the bottom
of the ninth off Mike Mohler (1-9) scored Fernando Vina with
the winning run as the Brewers edged the Oakland Athletics
